comparator.name: Frisian Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target names the Frisian Language and Culture track within the 180-EC BA Nederlandse Talen en Culturen, so the exact target-specific track is reconstructed. The current 2026-2027 programme-specific TER defines the complete pathway for the cohort beginning in September 2026: a fixed 60-EC first year, a fixed 60-EC second year and a 60-EC third year containing a 30-EC minor, a 10-EC faculty-wide choice, a 10-EC thesis and a 10-EC internship. The first-year and third-year faculty-wide choices and the minor remain explicit choice space rather than being filled with invented content. The TER notes that the second- and third-year components for this new cohort will enter OCASYS in 2027-2028 and 2028-2029 respectively.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target explicitly names the Frisian Language and Culture route. The 2026-2027 TER recognizes this as the FTC track within BA Nederlandse Talen en Culturen and defines its separate course pathway, language outcomes, thesis language and field-specific second- and third-year requirements. The exact route is therefore selected independently of UCR fit.

alternatives.label: Language, multilingualism & society
alternatives.concept: Study language as a social and cultural practice through introductory Dutch, stylistics, psycholinguistics, rhetoric and communication, then connect it to multilingualism, identity, media, sociology, social change and language policy. This related-fields route has no Frisian proficiency sequence or Frisian-language academic work.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines language and communication, psycholinguistics, literature and media, sociology, modern history and politics. The label reflects that balance without implying Frisian proficiency or a Frisian-studies curriculum.
progression: Introductory history, sociology, rhetoric and brain-and-behaviour study precede advanced communication, psycholinguistics, media and social-theory work. All formal prerequisites and planned terms pass; nine courses are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & cultural identity
alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical and media forms create cultural meaning and express identity, memory and power, combining textual interpretation, stylistics, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, film and multimodal production. Frisian literary history and Frisian-language depth remain explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film, media and cultural identity; it does not claim Frisian literary or language proficiency.
alternatives.distinctness: The language-and-society and literature-and-media routes share 19 courses and each has 5 different courses / 37.5 EC. The second route shifts from Dutch, EU politics, modern sociology, social movements and applied civic research toward literary foundations, major traditions, empire, myth and adaptation.
progression: Literature, rhetoric, sociology, brain-and-behaviour and media foundations precede advanced psycholinguistics, literary interpretation, communication and media production. All formal prerequisites and planned terms pass; eight courses are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Regional politics, public culture & heritage
alternatives.concept: Study regional identity and minority-language questions through modern history, comparative politics, EU governance, sociology, social movements, public communication, museums, heritage ethics and cultural memory. The route examines the institutional and cultural setting around regional language policy but does not teach Frisian or reproduce Frisian history and culture as a cumulative specialist field.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is led by history, politics, sociology, communication, museums, heritage and public memory. The label describes that regional and public-cultural focus without presenting it as Frisian Language and Culture.
progression: Foundations in modern history, comparative politics, sociology and art history precede EU politics, qualitative research, museums, conflict, social theory, public communication, heritage and advanced humanities research. All formal prerequisites and planned terms pass; eleven courses are at 300 level.
alternatives.distinctness: The regional-politics and heritage route differs from the language-and-society route by 10 courses / 75 EC and from the literature-and-media route by 11 courses / 82.5 EC. It replaces language acquisition and much literary study with comparative politics, EU governance, conflict, museums, heritage ethics and historical research.

candidates.label: Frisian proficiency and field-specific Frisian studies
candidates.assessment: UCR offers one introductory Dutch course but no Frisian course, cumulative Frisian proficiency sequence, Old Frisian, Frisian linguistics, Frisian literary history, field internship or thesis in Frisian. General psycholinguistics, stylistics, literature and regional politics cannot be presented as Frisian studies.

selection.assessment: Three complete and genuinely different related-fields programmes are defensible: language, multilingualism and society; literature, media and cultural identity; and regional politics, public culture and heritage. All three pass the pairwise 30-EC floor. The language-specific Frisian direction was assessed separately and remains infeasible because UCR lacks Frisian and cumulative proficiency study; the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

blocks: Both address language acquisition and multilingualism; UCR provides general psycholinguistics rather than Frisian proficiency or field-specific methodology.
Both develop literary interpretation; UCR is comparative and does not provide Frisian-language literary training.
Both develop source-based research; the UCR seminar is comparative history rather than Frisian studies.
Both require advanced humanities interpretation and research; Groningen requires Frisian literature and linguistics coverage.

notes.text: Groningen Frisian Language and Culture combines cumulative Frisian proficiency with Frisian linguistics, literature, regional history and politics, research ateliers, an internship and a Frisian-focused thesis. UCR can build coherent related programmes in language and multilingual society, literature and cultural identity, or regional politics and heritage, but these are not Frisian-language degree pathways.

UCR offers introductory Dutch but no Frisian course and no cumulative proficiency sequence, Old Frisian, Frisian phonology and syntax, Frisian literary history, field-based Frisian practice or thesis in Frisian. General psycholinguistics, stylistics, literature, media, history, politics and heritage remain related perspectives rather than substitutes.
